draft.title: Climate change as a sustainability challenge
card: Burning fossil fuels such as coal, oil and gas releases greenhouse gases, mainly carbon dioxide. These gases trap heat in the atmosphere.
As more heat is trapped, the average temperature of the planet rises. This is global warming, and it changes the climate over decades.
Warming can bring more extreme weather, such as heatwaves, heavy rain and bushfire weather. It also melts ice and warms the ocean, which raises sea level.

Ecosystems are harmed when temperatures, rainfall or ocean conditions change faster than species can adapt. This is a sustainability challenge because it threatens the needs of people today and in the future.
draft.remember: More greenhouse gases from fossil fuels trap more heat, and the warming harms people and ecosystems.

a.q: Why does burning fossil fuels contribute to global warming?
opts: It releases greenhouse gases that trap heat
It uses up oxygen that cools the atmosphere
It makes the sun deliver more heat to Earth
It melts polar ice, which then heats the air
a.why: Burning coal, oil and gas releases greenhouse gases such as carbon dioxide, which trap heat in the atmosphere. Melting ice is an effect of warming, not its cause, so the last option reverses cause and effect.
a.clue: Think about what is released when fuel burns.

b.q: Tui lives on a low coral island in the Pacific. Which change linked to climate change most directly raises the risk of flooding on her island?
opts: Sea level rise from melting ice and warmer oceans
More carbon dioxide being released by local cars
Fewer species living in the nearby coral reef
Hotter days that dry out the island's soil
b.why: Melting ice and warming ocean water raise sea level, and a low island has little height to spare. Harm to the reef is also an effect of climate change, but it is not what raises sea level.
b.clue: Which effect changes the height of the water?

a.best: It releases greenhouse gases that trap heat

b.best: Sea level rise from melting ice and warmer oceans

problems.detail: Why (a) calls the melting-ice option 'the last option', but the options appear in random order and it is the third one here. A student reading the explanation could be pointed to the wrong option. Name the option by its content instead.

For Year 12 HSC this question is very easy. Three distractors (the sun delivering more heat, using up cooling oxygen, melting ice heating the air) are plainly wrong to a student at this level, so the question tests little beyond Year 7–8 understanding.
